sections.overview: Iphiclides podalirius, the Scarce Swallowtail, is a large, long-tailed butterfly of warm parts of Europe and western Asia.
sections.identification: Adults have pale yellow wings crossed by bold black stripes and long hindwing tails.
sections.habitat: It favours warm, open or semi-open places with shrubs, including dry slopes, woodland edges, orchards and gardens.
sections.diet: Caterpillars feed on woody Rosaceae, especially blackthorn and mahaleb cherry in central Europe; adults take flower nectar.
sections.behavior: The butterfly is a strong flier and often glides, sometimes covering substantial distances.
sections.reproduction: Females lay eggs singly on host shrubs; in much of central Europe, low-growing blackthorn is a major host plant.
sections.ecology: The similar Iphiclides feisthamelii replaces it across Iberia and parts of the western Mediterranean; sources differ on whether feisthamelii is a species or subspecies.
sections.conservation: This profile describes a broad range; local status varies, and the sources consulted do not provide a current global category.
